glu-001.voice: I want to grow spiritually without the hard part.
glu-001.situation: Wanting the harvest of a disciplined life without the work of self-denial.
glu-001.note: In the Greek Bible Evagrius read, Issachar sees that the land is good and bends his shoulder to farm it.

glu-002.voice: Fasting gets you nothing. It won’t make you any holier.
glu-002.situation: Doubting that self-denial does your soul any real good.
glu-002.note: Evagrius’s Greek text says the bronze washing basin was made from the mirrors of women who fasted at the tent’s door. Their discipline became part of God’s house.

glu-003.voice: It’s a special day, and you’re run down anyway. Indulge.
glu-003.situation: Using a holiday or feeling unwell as the reason to give in to a craving.

excerpt.from: You will not eat just one day

glu-004.voice: Eat until you’re full. What harm could it do?
glu-004.situation: Filling up without noticing how comfort makes you forget God.

excerpt.from: you shall eat and be full

glu-005.voice: God asks too much. Fasting is a burden.
glu-005.situation: Feeling that God’s call to self-control is too heavy for you.

glu-006.voice: Food and drink can’t hurt your soul.
glu-006.situation: Assuming indulgence has no effect on your life with God.

glu-007.voice: You’ve fasted long enough. Eat now. Don’t wait for evening.
glu-007.situation: Wanting to break a fast before the time you set.
glu-007.note: Desert monks usually ate in mid-afternoon (the “ninth hour”). Here the pull is to eat at the usual time on a day set aside for a longer fast.

glu-008.voice: You’re going to run out of what you need.
glu-008.situation: Fear that your food, money or supplies are about to run dry.

glu-009.voice: I can follow the saints and keep every comfort too.
glu-009.situation: Wanting a holy life without giving anything up.
glu-009.note: Micaiah told the king the truth and was given the “bread of affliction” for it.

glu-010.voice: There isn’t enough to share with everyone who comes.
glu-010.situation: Holding back hospitality because you’re afraid there won’t be enough.

glu-011.voice: Living with this little is bitter. You deserve better.
glu-011.situation: Resentment about being poor or having little.

glu-012.voice: Better stock up on more. For guests, of course.
glu-012.situation: Hoarding more than you need and calling it hospitality.

glu-013.voice: Worry about what to eat and wear. The truth can wait.
glu-013.situation: Busy with food and clothes while ignoring what is wrong in your heart.

glu-014.voice: Ease up. All this fasting and work will wear out your body.
glu-014.situation: Being told your discipline is too hard on your weak body.

glu-015.voice: Don’t push yourself so hard staying up to pray.
glu-015.situation: Pressure to drop the late-night or early-morning prayer you committed to.

glu-016.voice: Where is your next meal coming from? You’d better figure it out.
glu-016.situation: Anxious scheming about how to get food, drink or money.

glu-017.voice: Staying awake to pray just stirs up more thoughts.
glu-017.situation: Feeling that praying at night only brings more distraction.

glu-018.voice: Giving that up is ridiculous. Nobody lives like that.
glu-018.situation: Being mocked or second-guessed for giving something up.

glu-019.voice: Keep fasting like this and you’ll ruin your health.
glu-019.situation: Fear that your discipline will harm you, or even kill you.

glu-020.voice: Skip prayer tonight. Your body needs the rest.
glu-020.situation: Talking yourself out of a prayer commitment for the sake of comfort.

glu-021.voice: Hard times are coming. You won’t make it.
glu-021.situation: Dread that famine, recession or disaster is just around the corner.

glu-022.voice: Have a drink. Water alone isn’t good for you.
glu-022.situation: Justifying alcohol as healthier than going without.
glu-022.note: This line appears only in the Greek version of Proverbs.

glu-023.voice: Plan your next meal. Growing in virtue can wait.
glu-023.situation: Thinking more about food than about becoming a better person.

glu-024.voice: Plain food again? This is miserable.

glu-025.voice: It’s a holiday. Be kind to yourself and have something nice.
glu-025.situation: Treating a celebration as permission to indulge.

glu-026.voice: You’ll get stomach trouble without a little wine.
glu-026.situation: Inventing health reasons to drink when you aren’t sick.

glu-027.voice: Swear you’ll never eat that again. Make a vow.
glu-027.situation: Binding yourself with rash vows about fasting or dieting.

glu-028.voice: They can get help somewhere else. It’s not your job.
glu-028.situation: Holding back food or help from someone in need.

glu-029.voice: You almost never indulge. Once in a long while is fine.
glu-029.situation: A gentle suggestion that a rare binge doesn’t count.

glu-030.voice: Remember those great evenings with good wine?
glu-030.situation: Nostalgia for past drinking and good times at the table.

glu-031.voice: Fill your stomach, even if it’s only bread and water.
glu-031.situation: The urge to eat until you are full, even of simple food.
glu-031.note: The source of this quotation is uncertain. It closely matches the Greek of Proverbs 24:15.

glu-032.voice: You’d be embarrassed not to go along with them.
glu-032.situation: Pressure to drop a commitment because refusing feels awkward in front of people you respect.
glu-032.note: The text of this entry may be damaged in the manuscripts. The verse distinguishes good shame from bad.

glu-033.voice: You’ve been strict for so long. Food can’t hurt you now.
glu-033.situation: Flattering promises that you’ve earned the right to indulge freely.

glu-034.voice: God’s commands only bring you hardship and misery.
glu-034.situation: Seeing God’s commands as harsh rather than loving.

glu-035.voice: Wine was made for people. Enjoy it.
glu-035.situation: Arguing that a good gift is always meant to be used right now.

glu-036.voice: Go back to how things used to be: the parties, the drinks.
glu-036.situation: Longing to return to old habits of feasting and drinking.

glu-037.voice: Go further. Live rough, cut everyone off, prove your devotion.
glu-037.situation: Being pushed toward extreme austerity and isolation beyond what is wise.

glu-038.voice: Remember how good life used to be? Look at it now.
glu-038.situation: Comparing a hard present with comfortable memories.

glu-039.voice: Picture the full table back home with family.
glu-039.situation: Daydreaming about a place of comfort and plenty you have left behind.

glu-040.voice: Everyone else is feasting and celebrating without you.
glu-040.situation: Feeling left out while others enjoy food and celebration.

glu-041.voice: A life of pleasure is better than this life of faith.
glu-041.situation: Calling indulgence good and the way of discipline bad.

glu-042.voice: I’m so tired of going without.
glu-042.situation: Weariness after a long stretch of having little.

glu-043.voice: My body is worn out, and my mind is full of impure thoughts.
glu-043.situation: Physically drained and still tempted, and asking God to remember you.

glu-044.voice: I feel weak and sick, like I’m wasting away.
glu-044.situation: Sudden physical weakness and distress, brought to God.

glu-045.voice: Bread and water aren’t enough. I want something more.
glu-045.situation: Not content with simple food and wanting extras.

glu-046.voice: How can I stand firm when temptation hits?
glu-046.situation: Looking for strength against temptation. Jesus prepared by fasting.

glu-047.voice: You have to worry. Guests, illness and hard times are coming.
glu-047.situation: Anxiety about food and clothing dressed up as being responsible.

glu-048.voice: Treat yourself well and life will go well.
glu-048.situation: Believing that comfort and pleasure are the road to a good life.

glu-049.voice: There’s not enough for both of you, and they’re probably lazy anyway.
glu-049.situation: Finding reasons not to share with someone in need.

glu-050.voice: Look after yourself first. Keep it for you.
glu-050.situation: Gathering food and goods for yourself alone.

glu-051.voice: This hardship is wearing me down.
glu-051.situation: Growing weary under the strain of self-restraint.

glu-052.voice: Take care of yourself. Eat and drink a little more.
glu-052.situation: Using self-care as cover for indulging.

glu-053.voice: Just a small treat. It’s only something little.
glu-053.situation: Wanting a small comfort food to console yourself.
glu-053.note: For desert monks who lived on bread and water, cooked vegetables were a treat.

glu-054.voice: It’s the season for it. You have to have some.
glu-054.situation: Seasonal cravings that feel impossible to pass up.

glu-055.voice: You’re in real need. Ease off; you can’t keep this up.

glu-056.voice: Your stomach, your liver… something is seriously wrong.
glu-056.situation: Imagining illness and fixating on symptoms.

glu-057.situation: Distress as your body ages or declines.

glu-058.voice: Why did you give that away? You’ll regret it.
glu-058.situation: Regret or annoyance after being generous.

glu-059.voice: You’ll make yourself sick. Eat a proper meal.
glu-059.situation: Fear of weakness used to make you break a commitment.

glu-060.voice: It’s a celebration. Get a little drunk.
glu-060.situation: Wanting to drink heavily on a holiday or special occasion.

glu-061.voice: Don’t work for it, and don’t ask family. Let others cover you.
glu-061.situation: Anxious maneuvering about how your needs will be met.

glu-062.voice: You’ll go hungry, or worse, have to accept charity.
glu-062.situation: Fear of need, and of the humiliation of receiving help.

glu-063.voice: Why work with your hands? Others will provide.
glu-063.situation: Avoiding honest work and expecting others to support you.

excerpt.from: that you make it your ambition

glu-064.voice: Skip the work. Just eat and fill up.

glu-065.voice: This discipline is cruel and does nothing for your soul.
glu-065.situation: Feeling that a disciplined life is all pain and no gain.

glu-066.voice: Focus on your meals. Other people’s needs aren’t your problem.
glu-066.situation: Caring about your own food while neglecting people in need.

glu-067.voice: Even Paul told Timothy to drink a little wine.
glu-067.situation: Quoting Scripture to justify drinking when you aren’t ill.
glu-067.note: Paul’s advice was for Timothy’s frequent illnesses. Evagrius aims the verse at a thought that borrows the permission without the illness.

glu-068.voice: Go back to the world and its ways. They’re not so bad.
glu-068.situation: Being drawn back toward the world’s way of living.

glu-069.voice: Fasting is too hard. God can’t really expect this.
glu-069.situation: Feeling that self-denial is an impossible burden.
